content.comment_body: Is it possible for a [product_name] module to use MQTT directly with a Raspberry Pi? From what I understand, currently the only supported option is connecting through AWS. AWS has proven to be very expensive for us, and their billing models are hard to understand. Currently, to monitor two [product_name] modules with around 50 values (both digital and analog), and with settings that report changes in value, our monthly bills are about £10 (UK) even with an E2C instance. Most costs seem to come from IoT messages and other AWS services we've used. We previously completed a project requiring remote visibility for a year, but going forward, we may discontinue using this platform due to the high costs. Our older solution using a remote connectivity device was much more affordable. If [company_name] wants to make cloud features truly practical, they should provide clearer guidance on pricing, examples of AWS packages, and also tools to monitor and limit MQTT messages in order to reduce expenses. This platform shows a lot of promise; we hope the usage costs become more manageable.
Direct MQTT connection from [product_name] modules is not possible. However, solutions like Node-RED or IOBroker can act as gateways.

analysis.insight_summary: Users express concern over high and unclear costs related to integrating [product_name] modules with AWS for cloud monitoring, noting a need for better cost transparency, monitoring tools, and improved MQTT connectivity options. Another user clarifies that direct MQTT connections between [product_name] and a Raspberry Pi are not currently supported, but external gateways provide alternatives. The conversation highlights unmet demands for flexible and cost-effective remote monitoring solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are looking for straightforward, affordable remote monitoring options from [product_name] devices, with clear pricing information, native support for MQTT connectivity, and tools to track and control message usage.
